The activity trend correlates directly with Ir utilization efficiency (Fig.3b, inset: At $<24\mathrm{w t}\%$ , incomplete $\mathsf{T i O}_{\mathsf{x}}@\mathsf{T i}$ surface coverage limits active site exposure; at >24 wt%, Ir nanoparticle agglomeration shields internal particles, reducing accessible active sites.

To probe the structural stability under harsh acidic OER conditions, inductively coupled plasma optical emission spectroscopy (ICP.OES) was employed to quantify Ir dissolution during electrolysis. As shown in Fig. 3c,$\mathrm{Ir/TiO_{x}@Ti}$ iexhibits a rapid initial dissolution phase (0-2h) followed by stabilization210h, total dissolution:.16mg/L),whereas unsupported Ir NPs show continuous dissolution over 8h (total dissolution: 0.6lmg/L). This 3.8-fold reduction in Ir leaching highlights the $\mathsf{T i O}_{\mathsf{x}}@\mathsf{T i}$ i support's critical role in anchoring Ir NPs and suppressing corrosion. Long-term chronopotentiometric testing at 10 mA/cm2 further reveals durabillity.$\mathsf{I r}/\mathsf{T i O}_{\mathsf{x}}@\mathsf{T i}$ undergoes an initial 10-hour activation phase, likely due to surface reconstruction into another active phase, and subsequently maintains stable operation for over 1700 h without degradation (Fig. 3d and Supplementary Fig. 15).

The operational stability of $\mathrm{Ir/TiO_{x}@Ti-based}$ PEMWEs was evaluated via chronopotentiometry at industrially relevant current densities $(1-2\mathrm{A}/\mathrm{cm}^{2}$ , Fig.7d). The cell exhibits very low voltage degradation over 400 h at both 1A/cm (degradation rate: 22 μV/h,Figs.7e) and 2 A/cm (degradation rate: 52 μV/h), achieving an 89%reduction in degradation rate compared to unsupported Ir NPs (460 V/h). Additionally, commercial Ir black and $\mathrm{IrO_{2}/TiO_{2}}$ catalysts were tested. Under low Ir loadings,$\mathsf{I r}/\mathsf{T i O}_{\mathsf{x}}@\mathsf{T i}$ still demonstrates markedly higher activity and stability advantages compared to both commercial Ir black and $\mathrm{IrO}_{2}/\mathrm{TiO}_{2}$ (Supplementary Figs. 39 and 4O).
